inline_text:
Replaces the "Write-once-read-many storage semantics for the evidence store" clause in the E4 use case with a requirement that keeps tamper-evidence and states a retention basis.

The clause cannot coexist with the sentence next to it, "Authorization and approval chain records (who/what approved each consequential action)". An approval record identifies a person. Write-once storage forbids deletion by construction. Under GDPR that store cannot be operated lawfully in the EU: Art 17(1) gives erasure, Art 5(1)(e) limits storage to what the purpose requires, Art 17(3) suspends erasure only for a legal obligation or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims. Recital 26 makes a linkable hash personal data. The AI Act retention floors at Art 19(1) for providers and Art 26(6) for deployers require keeping records long enough rather than keeping identifiers indefinitely.

The replacement sentence:

"Tamper-evident storage with a declared retention basis: integrity of the record must remain verifiable without requiring personal identifiers to be retained beyond the period their legal basis permits. Where an identifier is removed under policy, the record carries a typed tombstone, so a verifier can distinguish an expired record from one that never carried the field."

What changes and what does not:

- Integrity stays verifiable. Chain-linking plus an external timestamp proves the bytes did not change without freezing them past the point where a deletion duty attaches.
- The retention period becomes explicit rather than implied, so a verifier can check expiry instead of inferring it.
- The tombstone is the part that matters in practice. Without it, a verifier cannot tell "identifier removed under policy" from "identifier never present". Only one of those is innocent.
- One sentence changes. The rest of the paragraph, including the capability and ladder requirements, is untouched, so this reads as a correction rather than a rewrite.

Scope note. The clause came in with the original E4 contribution in 12928d16, so this is a correction of our own text rather than a change to someone else's. The matching schema question, a `retention` block and a pseudonymisation hook in the record format, is raised in #37 and will travel as a diff against a 0.2 draft rather than an edit to the published 0.1.

Raised in #37 by @smcd and written up in comment 6541798008. @mr-lee @91pavan @StevenMih for review and merge.
